label: Resilience enclaves + bio/cyber civil defence
summary: Hardened biosecurity infrastructure (wastewater/metagenomic surveillance, PPE stockpiles, isolated backup food/power/communications systems) built out in anticipation of AI-enabled bio or cyber attacks, similar in spirit to civil-defence programs.

source.quote: Curator-drafted intervention: bundles biosecurity civil-defence proposals discussed in the pandemic-preparedness and AI-safety literature (e.g. Nucleic Acid Observatory-style early-warning systems, critical-infrastructure hardening) into one representative nudge.

cost.note: Low-to-moderate direct fiscal cost relative to other interventions here: mostly public-health and infrastructure-hardening spending that does not require new international coordination or new taxing authority.

nudges.evidence: Early-warning surveillance and hardened infrastructure directly reduce the odds a bio or cyber attack reaches catastrophic (1M+ death or weeks-long outage) scale, though they cannot fully prevent an attack from being attempted.

Visible civil-defence hardening modestly lowers the odds that a catastrophic attack cascades into direct great-power conflict, by reducing the perceived payoff of an attack and giving states more time to de-escalate.

Civil-defence infrastructure (biometric screening, population monitoring for early warning) has some dual-use surveillance potential; the same systems that detect a bioweapon can be repurposed for population control if institutions are not careful.
